summary: Suspected NCCL collective stall in TP workloads — guidance on timeout settings + timeline for runtime fixes
body:
Customer: Crestwell Analytics (Dedicated, EU-West)

Issue summary
- Customer reports intermittent request timeouts / hangs when running TP=8 on multi-GPU nodes. Symptom looks like a stalled NCCL collective: tokens stop streaming, GPU utilization drops unevenly across ranks, and requests eventually hit gateway timeout.
- Customer is requesting (1) recommended timeout settings / immediate mitigations and (2) timeline for Redwood’s longer-term fixes (watchdog + async error propagation) and how they will be rolled out.

Impact
- User-visible: streaming responses hang mid-generation; client retries cause burst load.
- Platform-visible: increased 504s at the edge + elevated in-flight request age on the dedicated pool.
- Frequency: customer reports 2–5 occurrences/day during peak batch ingestion.

Environment (per customer)
- Deployment: Dedicated
- Region: eu-west
- Node shape: 8x GPU per host (TP=8)
- Runtime version: 1.18.3 (customer-provided)
- Workload pattern: high concurrency + long streams (2–6 min), mixed prompt lengths, some client disconnects

Customer-provided indicators
- "NCCL call appears stuck; no explicit error surfaced. One rank appears to lag then whole group stops making progress." (verbatim)

What we asked for (to confirm signature)
- Timestamp window(s) with request IDs
- Runtime logs around collectives / cancellation
- Whether client disconnects are common (mobile / proxy timeouts)
- Any changes to driver/CUDA/NCCL in the last 2 weeks

---

Support / Engineering notes (internal)
Hypothesis
- Matches known TP hang class we’ve been tracking: collective async errors not surfacing promptly + barrier/cancellation edge cases causing a TP group to stop making forward progress.
- In 1.18.x the failure mode can present as a “silent stall” (no hard crash) until downstream timeouts trip.

Quick checks performed (Redwood side)
- SRE looked at customer’s dedicated dashboards during provided time window:
  - p99 streaming duration increased sharply, then plateaued.
  - TP-group resets absent (watchdog not enabled in their current runtime).
  - Scheduler showed growing queue depth but stable host health.

Immediate mitigation guidance provided (2025-02-21)
1) Reduce stall blast radius by lowering max in-flight per TP group
- Recommended config (temporary):
  - max_concurrent_streams_per_tp_group: 2 (from 4)
  - max_inflight_requests_per_host: -20% from current

2) Ensure NCCL async error handling is enabled (if not already)
- Set (host env): NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
- Set (host env): NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1
Note: This can convert some “hangs” into surfaced errors (fail-fast), which is preferable operationally; Redwood will then quarantine/reset the TP group when watchdog is available.

3) Increase collective timeout to avoid premature aborts while we gather evidence (balanced recommendation)
- For their workload (long streams), recommended increasing NCCL_TIMEOUT from default to 180–240 seconds.
- If they see more frequent aborts after enabling async handling, adjust to 240s.

4) If hangs correlate with client disconnects, reduce disconnect-driven cancellation pressure
- Customer to confirm whether upstream proxy enforces aggressive idle timeouts.
- Suggested increasing client / proxy idle timeout to >= 120s during streaming.

5) Provide a safe “escape hatch” while debugging
- If incident repeats during business hours, temporarily route to non-TP model variant / smaller model (if acceptable) or reduce max output tokens.

Customer questions answered
Q: "Should we increase or decrease NCCL timeout?"
A: Increase moderately (180–240s) to reduce false aborts, but enable NCCL async error handling so real faults don’t present as silent stalls. Longer term, Redwood runtime will enforce its own TP-group watchdog with safer defaults.

Q: "Is this a known issue / do you have a fix?"
A: Yes, this maps to an active runtime stability initiative. Fixes are landing in runtime 1.19 (collective async error propagation + TP-group watchdog/quarantine + cancellation-safe barriers). We can provide a hotfix build for Dedicated once canary results are clean.

Q: "When will this be rolled out to Dedicated?"
A: Plan shared with customer:
- Hosted canary: Week of 2025-02-24 (nightly perf-canary + targeted high-load pools)
- Dedicated opt-in: starting 2025-03-03 for a small set of affected customers (including Crestwell) pending canary gates
- Default-on: after ~1–2 weeks of stable results (tentative mid-March), with an opt-out flag if needed
(Exact dates subject to go/no-go; Connor O’Brien owns release coordination.)

---

Timeline / comments

2025-02-21 09:14 (Owen Phillips, Support)
- Opened ticket after customer escalation via support portal. Requested timestamps, request IDs, and confirmation of runtime version + GPU type.

2025-02-21 10:02 (Dev Patel, Support Escalation)
- Acknowledged suspected NCCL collective stall signature; provided immediate mitigations (enable NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING / BLOCKING_WAIT, adjust NCCL_TIMEOUT, reduce concurrency per TP group). Linked customer to known-issues page and asked for a 30-minute window with 3–5 request IDs.

2025-02-22 08:47 (Customer)
- Confirmed client disconnects occur (internal job runner enforces a 60s idle timeout during streaming; may cut connections mid-generation). Provided two request IDs and a timestamp window (approx 07:55–08:10 UTC).

2025-02-22 12:30 (Dev Patel)
- Advised increasing the job runner idle timeout to >= 120s and/or using non-streaming for long generations in batch jobs as a temporary mitigation. Noted that cancellation/disconnect paths are part of the 1.19 fix set.

2025-02-24 16:05 (Rafael Mendes, SRE)
- Reviewed eu-west dedicated metrics: saw a pattern consistent with comm stall vs kernel stall (collective latency spikes without corresponding kernel time increase). Recommended we prioritize them for 1.19 Dedicated opt-in once available.

2025-02-26 11:18 (Dev Patel)
- Shared preliminary rollout notes (runtime 1.19 candidate includes: periodic async error checks, per-TP-group forward-progress watchdog, quarantine + controlled teardown). Referenced PRs: 18455/18462/18473. Offered scheduling a 30-min technical check-in to validate configs.

2025-03-01 07:40 (Customer)
- Reported improvements after enabling NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and increasing idle timeout; still saw one hang under peak load.

2025-03-03 10:25 (Dev Patel)
- Confirmed Crestwell added to Dedicated opt-in list for runtime 1.19.x TP stability patch. Provided final recommended interim settings:
  - NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
  - NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1
  - NCCL_TIMEOUT=240
  - Reduce per-TP-group concurrent streams to 2 until patched runtime is deployed
- Asked customer to notify support if hangs continue post-upgrade; requested they keep a sample request ID list for validation.

Resolution
- Resolved as “mitigations provided + upgrade scheduled.” Customer confirmed immediate mitigations reduced frequency; Dedicated opt-in to runtime 1.19.x planned with SRE guardrails.

Next steps / follow-ups
- Support: coordinate upgrade window + confirm post-upgrade behavior (Dev Patel)
- SRE: ensure dashboard panels/alerts for watchdog triggers are enabled for this cluster (INT-611 tracking)
- Runtime Eng: ensure 1.19.x patch includes dedicated-safe defaults and release notes cover timeout knob guidance

Customer-facing notes (what to tell them)
- This is a known TP stability issue class in sustained multi-GPU workloads; Redwood has fixes landing in runtime 1.19 with watchdog/quarantine and improved NCCL async error surfacing.
- Short-term: keep async error handling enabled, increase idle timeout for streaming, set NCCL_TIMEOUT to 240s for long generations, and cap concurrent streams per TP group until patch is deployed.
